title: Applied Relationships Between Measurements
introduction: Explore applied relationships between measurements using everyday examples.
definition: Use given relationships between length, mass and liquid volume in practical problems, without treating unlike units as interchangeable. A stated rate such as grams per metre or millilitres per container links quantities.

examples.question: A cable has mass 250 g per metre. Find mass of 6 m.

exercises.question: A rope weighs 200 g per metre. Mass of 4 m in g?
A bottle holds 750 mL. Six bottles hold how many mL?
3 kg of material is split into 250 g portions. Number?
Each metre of pipe holds 2 L. 7 m holds L?
A liquid has mass 800 g per L. Mass of 2 L in g?
A 5 L container fills 250 mL cups. Number?
Six bottles each contain 750 mL. Find total in L.
Find the mass in kg of 12 packs of 350 g.

summary: Use given relationships between length, mass and liquid volume in practical problems, without treating unlike units as interchangeable. A stated rate such as grams per metre or millilitres per container links quantities.
